standard.title: Developing Geographical Inquiry Questions
standard.description: develop a range of questions for a geographical inquiry related to a phenomenon or challenge
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can develop geographical questions to guide inquiry and plan investigations at a range of scales (Y7-8). They are building towards refining questions using geographical concepts and multi-scale digital planning tools. At Y9, the move is from generating initial questions to sharpening focus through geographical concepts and scale.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop and modify a range of questions that sharpen the focus of a geographical inquiry using concepts and scale, and plan an investigation using digital tools.

nodes.label: Generating initial inquiry questions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a range of questions to investigate why a geographical phenomenon has changed or why a challenge has arisen
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least three questions that investigate a geographical phenomenon or challenge from different angles (e.g. what, why, how, who is affected)
nodes.typical_width: Develop a range of questions for a geographical inquiry that investigate causes, impacts, connections and management dimensions of a phenomenon or challenge; ensure questions are open and investigable
wider: Evaluate a set of questions for geographical focus — identify which questions are genuinely geographical and which are too general or not investigable
Develop questions for both a biome and an interconnections topic — compare how the same question types operate differently across different phenomena
Develop questions at different levels of complexity — identify which questions scaffold the investigation and which are the driving research question
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot generate a range of investigable questions from different angles, they cannot refine and sharpen these into a coherent inquiry plan in Node 2. A single question or description-only questions collapse the inquiry into a report task and block all subsequent phases of work.

response_modes.reason: Question generation is a procedural capability that improves with practice across multiple phenomena. Students who develop questions for only one topic have a fragile repertoire. Building range across biome and interconnection topics — as the elaborations suggest — ensures the capability transfers.

success_criteria: Develops at least three questions that investigate different dimensions of a phenomenon or challenge
Questions are open and investigable (not yes/no)
Questions address at least two of: causes, impacts, connections, management

nodes.label: Sharpening questions using concepts and scale
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can modify questions to sharpen the focus of an investigation using geographical concepts or scale of study
nodes.minimum_width: Modify at least one question from Node 1 to sharpen its focus using a geographical concept (e.g. scale, interconnection, sustainability) or a specified scale of study
nodes.typical_width: Develop and modify questions to sharpen inquiry focus by integrating geographical concepts and specifying scale (e.g. national scale, local scale); show how the modified question produces a more focused investigation than the original
wider: Compare how the same question operates differently at local versus global scale — explain what changes and what stays the same
Modify a broad question into a sequence of focused sub-questions that could structure an investigation
Evaluate the difference between concept-sharpened and content-narrowed questions — explain why adding a geographical concept produces a different kind of question than narrowing to a specific example
nodes.hinge_reason: Questions that lack geographical concept focus or clear scale produce unfocused investigations. If students cannot sharpen a question, their planning in Node 3 will lack the disciplinary focus needed to select appropriate tools and sources. An unsharpened question makes the investigation plan arbitrary.

response_modes.reason: Question modification is a metacognitive move — students must reflect on what their original question is actually asking, identify what is missing (geographical concept, scale specification), and reconstruct it. Scaffolding the diagnostic step — 'what is this question missing?' — builds the reflective reasoning the modification requires.

success_criteria: Modifies at least one question to include a geographical concept or scale specification
Explains how the modification sharpens the inquiry focus
Produces a question that is more focused and investigable than the original

nodes.label: Planning a multi-scale investigation using digital tools
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan an investigation of a geographical phenomenon using digital tools at a range of scales
nodes.minimum_width: Outline an investigation plan that identifies: the phenomenon, the scale(s) of study, at least two digital tools to be used, and what data or information will be collected
nodes.typical_width: Plan a geographical investigation of a biome modification or place connection topic using digital tools; specify the scale(s) of investigation, the tools to be used (e.g. GIS, mapping platforms, digital data sources), and how the investigation will address the sharpened questions from Node 2
wider: Develop an investigation plan that uses different digital tools for different scales — explain why each tool is appropriate for its scale
Anticipate methodological challenges in the plan — what data might be difficult to find, what scale transitions are problematic?
Evaluate two possible investigation plans for the same question — explain which is more feasible and would produce better geographical data

response_modes.reason: The investigation plan integrates the sharpened questions from Nodes 1-2 with tool selection and scale decisions. Teaching investment should focus on the connection: the digital tools chosen should be appropriate for the scale and the question type, not selected arbitrarily. A plan where tool choice is disconnected from the question has not reached this checkpoint.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The plan evaluation direction is rich — comparing two possible plans for the same question requires students to apply feasibility, quality and geographical rigour criteria simultaneously. Advancing students who evaluate plans develop methodological judgement that transfers across all S-strand tasks.
success_criteria: Identifies the phenomenon, scale(s) and digital tools in an investigation plan
Connects tool selection to the scale and question type
Explains how the plan addresses the sharpened questions from Node 2
